first.rationale: A tightly targeted SMB pricing test most directly addresses competitive displacement and has prior evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. Verify its durability, qualification, and margin effects before launch; also verify onboarding evidence because the completion decline could reduce the value of newly acquired accounts. Restrict eligibility and evaluate qualified revenue, retention, and realized margin rather than conversion alone.

mid.rationale: Run a shortened-onboarding experiment. Its archived result directly addresses the 4% completion decline and showed higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and a 3% 30-day retention lift, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its apparent revenue gain came with a 12% retention decline before renewal. Measure first meaningful action, qualified conversion, retention, and realized revenue by SMB cohort.

final2.rationale: Keep the experiment on shortened onboarding: it is the only direction with verified evidence of improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, directly addressing the current activation and completion declines. Do not launch deeper promotional pricing as the experiment; the verified SMB discount increased acquisition but reduced 30-day retention by 12%, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. The acute price-driven churn risk remains material, so monitor price-sensitive SMB churn separately and avoid inferring that an acquisition discount would retain the installed base.
